editorial:
Imagine being the best hitman in the world, only to find out you are dying. That is exactly where Joe Flood finds himself. Instead of waiting around, he does something totally wild: he puts a bounty on his own head to make his final days a challenge. It sounds crazy, but it sets up a ride that is half non-stop fighting and half romantic comedy. You get to see Joe struggle with his health while trying to avoid a whole army of killers who are all trying to collect the prize money. The vibe is lighthearted and doesn't take itself too seriously, making it a great pick for a lazy weekend.

What really works here is the action. The fights are clean and fast, and the chemistry between the leads keeps you rooting for them. While the plot is a bit predictable, the pacing never slows down enough for you to get bored. If you love movies where the hero is outmatched but still finds a way to win, you will have a blast.
endingExplained: After a massive final battle with the other assassins, Joe manages to survive and save his ex-girlfriend. The big twist is that Joe's illness was actually a misdiagnosis, meaning he is not dying after all. He gets a second chance at life and a fresh start with the woman he loves. The movie ends on a happy note with Joe finally retiring from the killing business to live a normal, healthy life.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves high-energy action movies with a sense of humor.
